intended_object: The torus embedding T_N = Hom(M, ℂ^×) ↪ X_Σ of the dense torus into the toric variety of a fan Σ (here, its complex-analytic realization for a regular fan), given by t ↦ t · x_{0}, where x_{0} is the distinguished point (identity) of the zero-cone orbit. This comes from the docstring and the module doc (Fulton §3.1, CLS §§3.2–3.3).
explanation:
The definition maps a torus element `t : ComplexTorus N` to `t • analyticDistinguishedPoint ⟨⊥, _⟩`. Here `ComplexTorus N` is `AddChar (IntegralCharacter N) ℂˣ`, i.e. Hom(M, ℂ^×) ≅ N ⊗ ℂ^×, which is the standard coordinate-free torus. The distinguished point of the zero cone is x_{0}, the point whose monomial values are all 1 in every chart. The companion theorem `analyticTorusι_eq_analyticAffineChartι` confirms this: in every affine chart U_σ the map is t ↦ t·(1,…,1). This is exactly the standard orbit map of the identity point, i.e. the inclusion of the dense torus O(0) ≅ T_N into X_Σ.

The hypothesis `Nonempty Phi.cones` is only needed to produce the zero cone as a member of the fan. Regularity is needed only because the library builds `analyticRealization` for regular fans; that restriction belongs to the ambient construction, not to this map. Given that realization, the map is defined in its natural generality. Mathlib has no toric varieties, so it has no counterpart.
